landmarks.name: Sagrada Familia
landmarks.writeup: A large unfinished Roman Catholic basilica in Barcelona designed by architect Antoni Gaudí, known for its unique modernist architecture.

wiki.extract:
Basílica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família, or simply Sagrada Família, is a Catholic church under construction in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. Designed by the Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí, it is the tallest church 
in the world. On 7 November 2010, Pope Benedict XVI consecrated the church and proclaimed it a basilica. Parts of the Sagrada Família were declared as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005, under "Works of Antoni Gaudí".

landmarks.name: Alhambra
landmarks.writeup: A palace and fortress complex in Granada, showcasing Moorish architecture and rich Islamic art from the Nasrid dynasty.

wiki.extract: The Alhambra is a palatine city and fortress complex located in Granada, Spain. It is one of the most famous monuments of Islamic architecture and the only well-preserved palace from the medieval Islamic world. Additionally, the palace contains notable examples of Spanish Renaissance architecture.

landmarks.name: Prado Museum
landmarks.writeup: One of the world's premier art museums located in Madrid, housing European art from the 12th to early 20th century.

wiki.extract: The Museo del Prado, officially known as Museo Nacional del Prado, is the main Spanish national art museum, located in central Madrid. It houses collections of European art, dating from the 12th century to the early 20th century, based on the former Spanish royal collection, and the single best collection of Spanish art. Founded as a museum of paintings and sculpture in 1819, it also contains important collections of other types of works. The numerous works by Francisco Goya, the single most extensively represented artist, as well as by Hieronymus Bosch, El Greco, Peter Paul Rubens, Titian, and Diego Velázquez, are some of the highlights of the collection. Velázquez and his keen eye and sensibility were also responsible for bringing much of the museum's fine collection of Italian masters to Spain, now one of the largest outside of Italy.

landmarks.name: Park Güell
landmarks.writeup: A public park in Barcelona featuring colorful mosaics and architectural elements designed by Antoni Gaudí.

wiki.extract: Park Güell is a complex of parks and gardens in Barcelona with architectural elements, located in the La Salut neighborhood of the Gràcia district in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. It is situated on the southern slope of the Turó del Carmel hill, part of the Collserola mountain range, overlooking the city. The separate Parc del Carmel lies on the northern side of the same hill.

landmarks.name: Plaza Mayor
landmarks.writeup: A historic central square in Madrid, known for its symmetrical architecture and vibrant cultural events.

wiki.extract: The Plaza Mayor is the principal public square in the heart of Madrid, the capital of Spain. It was once the centre of Old Madrid. It was first built (1580–1619) during the reign of Philip III. Only a few blocks away is another famous plaza, the Puerta del Sol.

cultural_events.name: La Tomatina
cultural_events.writeup: An annual tomato-throwing festival held in Buñol, attracting participants worldwide for a playful food fight.

cultural_events.name: Running of the Bulls
cultural_events.writeup: Part of the San Fermín festival in Pamplona, where participants run in front of bulls through the city streets.

cultural_events.name: Fallas de Valencia
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional celebration in Valencia featuring large papier-mâché figures that are burned at the festival's end.

cultural_events.name: Semana Santa
cultural_events.writeup: Holy Week processions held across Spain, featuring elaborate floats and religious ceremonies.

cultural_events.name: Feria de Abril
cultural_events.writeup: A spring fair in Seville known for flamenco dancing, traditional costumes, and Andalusian culture.

food_writeup: Spanish cuisine is diverse, featuring dishes like paella, tapas, gazpacho, and jamón ibérico. It emphasizes fresh ingredients, olive oil, and regional flavors.
brief_history: Spain has a rich history influenced by Romans, Visigoths, Moors, and Christian kingdoms. It became a global empire in the 15th and 16th centuries and transitioned to democracy after Franco's dictatorship ended in 1975.

important_people.name: Miguel de Cervantes
important_people.description: Renowned writer, author of Don Quixote.

current_conflicts: Spain faces internal political tensions related to Catalan independence movements but is not involved in any active armed conflicts.
